questions.question: The average runs scored by Sunil in 17 innings is 37. What is his score in the 17th inning, thereby, increasing his average score by 9 runs?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average run scored by Sunil in 17 innings = 37.

**Formula used: **

Average = frac{ {sum of the all the observations}}{ {total no. of observations}}

**Calculation:**

Let Sunil's score in the 17th inning be x.

His average until the 16th inning was = 37 - 9 = 28.

Therefore, his total score after the 16th inning = 16 × 28

⇒ 448

Then, after the 17th inning,

⇒ ((16 × 28)+x)/(17) = the average of 17th inning

⇒ (16 × 28) + x = 37 × 17

⇒ 448 + x = 629

⇒ x = 629 - 448

⇒ x = 181

**∴ Sunil scored 181 runs in the 17th inning.**

questions.question: What is the volume of a right circular cylinder whose curved surface area is 12 π cm² and the circumference of its base is 4 π cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of right circular cylinder = 12 π cm². 

Circumference = 4 π cm2. 

**Formula Used:**

Curved surface area = 2 × πrh 

where, h = height of the cylinder, and r = radius of the cylinder.

Circumference = 2 × πr

The volume of the cylinder = πr²h

**CALCULATION:**

Circumference = 4 × π 

⇒ 2 × πr = 4 × π

⇒ r = 2 cm

Curved surface area = 12 × π

⇒ 2 × πrh = 12 × π

⇒ 2 × 2 × h = 12

⇒ h = 3 cm.

Now,

The volume of the cylinder = πr2h

Volume = π × (2)2 × 3

Volume = 12 π cm³

**∴ The volume of the right circular cylinder is 12 π cm3.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone of radius 28 cm is 4664 cm². What is the slant height of the cone?(Use π=22/7)
questions.solution:

radius = 28 cm

Curved surface area of cone = π × r × l

where l = slant height; r = radius

**Calculation:**

Curved surface area = 4664

⇒ π × r × l = 4664

⇒ 22/7 × 28 × l = 4664

⇒ l = 53 cm

**∴ Slant height i.e. l is 53 cm.**

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, CA is produced to P, ∠ BAP = 126°. If ∠ABC ∶ ∠ACB = 5 ∶ 2, the degree measures of ∠B and ∠C are respectively:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ BAP = 126° 

∠ABC : ∠ACB = 5 : 2

**Formula used:**

The sum of all the angles of a triangle is 180°

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° 

The sum of the angles in a straight line is 180° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd595cb30f9c254d1c1294136c986bbdc02286587a438b007bac6a28bb070fa9.png] 

Let ∠ABC = 5x; ∠ACB = 2x

As CA is produced to P 

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠BAP = 180° (sum of the angles in a straight line = 180° )

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° - ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° - 126° = 54° 

In △ ABC

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 5x + 2x + 54 = 180

⇒ 7x = 126 

⇒ x = 18** **

So, angle B = 5x = 5 × 18 = 90° 

Angle C = 2x = 2 × 18 = 36°

**∴ The correct answer is 90°, 36°.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

**Concept Used:**

The exterior angle theorem, 

According to the figure: 

We know that, 

∠ ABC + ∠ ACB = ∠ BAP

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd595cb30f9c254d1c1294136c986bbdc02286587a438b007bac6a28bb070fa9.png] 

⇒ ∠ ABC + ∠ ACB = ∠ BAP

⇒ 5x + 2x = 126°

⇒ 7x = 126°

⇒ x = 126°/7 = 18°

Now, 

∠ B = 5x = 5 × 18 = 90° 

∠ C = 2x = 2 × 18 = 36° 

∴ Angle B is 90° and angle C is 36° .

questions.question: When the price of a watch was reduced by 20%, the number of watches sold is increased by 40%. What was the effect on the sales in percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The price of a watch is reduced to 20%

The number of watches sold has increased by 40%

**Formula used:**

effective percentage change = x + y + (xy/100)

**Calculation:**

Since first it is reduced to 20% and then it has increased by 40%

Effective percentage change = - x + y - (xy/100) 

⇒ -20 +40 - 800/100 = +12

Here + sign shows an increase in the percentage

**∴ The effect on sales in percentage is a 12% increase.**

questions.question: Malay walks around a circular field at the rate of 7 rounds per hour, while Neha runs around it at the rate of 11 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 02:45 p.m. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Malay speed round a circular field = 7 rounds per hour.

Neha speed round a circular field = 11 rounds per hour

they start at 2:45 p.m. in the same direction. 

**FORMULA USED:**

Relative speeds when moving in the same direction = difference of speeds.

**CALCULATION :**

The relative speed between Malay and Neha = 11 - 7 = 4 rounds/h (as they are in the same direction )

Time taken to complete one round at this speed = 1/4 hr

⇒ (1/4) × 60 min

⇒ 15 min.

So, 2:45 + 15 min = 3:00 p.m.

**∴ They shall first cross each other after 15 minutes i.e. at 03:00 p.m.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work alone in 96 days and B can do it alone in 104 days. In how many days can the duo, working together, complete the work?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A does work in 96 days

B does work for 104 days 

**CONCEPT USED:**

No. of days = total work / efficiency 

**CALCULATION:**

Let us assume the total work to be L.C.M (96, 104) = 1248

Now, the efficiency of A = 1248/96 = 13 unit/days

Efficiency of B = 1248/104 = 12 unit /days

Now, the total efficiency of A and B = ( 12 + 13 ) = 25 unit /days 

Number of days in which A and B complete the work together

⇒ 1248 /25 = 49.92 days

**∴ In 49.92 days, both A and B together complete the work.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹20,000 for 9 months at the rate of 4% per annum, when interest is compounded quarterly?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Principal = Rs.20,000

Time = 9 months

Rate = 4% per annum

**FORMULA USED:**

C.I. = P × ( 1 +R/100)^t - P

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, t = time and C.I. = Compound Interest.

**CALCULATION:**

Since the interest is compounded quarterly:

Rate = (4/4) = 1 %; Time = 9 × 4 = 36 months = 3 years 

Now, 

⇒ C.I. = 20,000 × ( 1 +1/100)³ - 20,000

⇒ C.I. = {20,000 × 101/100 × 101/100 × 101/100} - 20,000

⇒ C.I. = (20,000 ×1030301/1000000) - 20,000

⇒ C.I. = Rs.606.02.

**∴ The Compound interest is Rs.606.02.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Concept used:

Effective rate for 3 years at the rate of a% = 3a + (3a²/100) + a³/10000

**Calculation:**

Since the interest is compounded quarterly:

Rate = (4/4) = 1 %; Time = 9 × 4 = 36 months = 3 years 

Effective rate for 3 years at the rate of a% = 3 × 1 + (3 × 1/100) + 1/10000

⇒ 3 + 0.03 + 0.0001 = 3.0301 %

Now,

⇒ C.I = 20000 × 3.0301% 

⇒ C.I = Rs.606.02.

∴ The Compound interest is Rs.606.02.

questions.question: A man bought a piece of land for ₹48,000. He sold two-fifth of it at a loss of 10%. At what gain percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) should he sell the remaining land to earn an overall profit of 42%?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Target profit units = 5 parts × 42% = 210%

Loss units from first part = 2 parts × (−10%) = −20%

Profit required from remaining 3 parts = 210% − (−20%) = 230%

Required gain % = 230% ÷ 3 = 76.66% ≈ 76.7%

**∴ The correct option is A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price (CP) = ₹48,000

Overall Profit % = 42%

First portion = 2/5 of the land sold at 10% loss

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) ÷ 100

Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 Total Land CP = ₹48,000

 Loss 10%
 3/5 Part
 Gain x%
 
• 
 Overall Target Profit = 42%

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 2/5 portion = 48,000 × (2 ÷ 5) = ₹19,200

⇒ SP of 2/5 portion at 10% loss = 19,200 × (90 ÷ 100) = ₹17,280

⇒ Desired overall SP for 42% profit = 48,000 × (142 ÷ 100) = ₹68,160

⇒ SP required from remaining 3/5 portion = 68,160 − 17,280 = ₹50,880

⇒ CP of remaining 3/5 portion = 48,000 − 19,200 = ₹28,800

⇒ Profit needed on remaining portion = 50,880 − 28,800 = ₹22,080

⇒ Required Gain % = (22,080 ÷ 28,800) × 100 = 76.666...%

⇒ Required Gain % ≈ 76.7%

**∴ The correct option is A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit

Overall profit or loss is the weighted average of individual profit/loss percentages: Pₜₒₜₐₗ = (w₁p₁ + w₂p₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Selling Price and Cost Price Relationship

SP = CP × (1 + Gain/100) for profit and SP = CP × (1 − Loss/100) for loss calculations.

Successive Percentage Changes

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.
